content: No direct, curated or published evidence that T-type (Cav3, CACNA1G/H/I) modulation is an antiseizure mechanism in WWOX deficiency.

note: Headline claim of the report; stated as an absence.

content: The dismech WOREE entry (about 1,800 lines) was searched for CACNA, T-type, Cav, calcium channel, ethosuximide; zero mechanistic or treatment matches.
note: Search is described as a grep of a knowledge-base file; the file itself is not identified.

content: Only curated drug-linked seizure mechanism in WWOX-DEE is GSK-3beta-dependent scaffold loss; lithium abolishes PTZ-induced seizures in Wwox-/- mice.
note: No primary PMID given for the lithium result.

content: Loss of the WWOX scaffold de-repressing GSK-3beta signalling is offered as the reading consistent with the lithium result.
note: Seizure-mechanism arm is called scaffold/GSK-3beta-centric.

content: A parallel PubMed search returned no WWOX-T-type association; 0 PubMed hits after multiple queries for a direct WWOX-Cav3 regulatory link.
note: Queries not listed.

content: Curated treatments in the knowledge base: conventional (often drug-resistant) antiseizure medication, AAV9-SynI-WWOX gene replacement, nutritional support, genetic counselling.
note: PMID attached to the AAV9 item.

content: The absence of any Cav3 node is meaningful, not an oversight of a thin entry; any T-type claim is exogenous to the disease model.
note: Rests on E02. Audit: the report's warrant adjectives for this absence are 'extensively validated' (L8) and 'deeply researched, ontology-harmonized' (L16); unverified report assertions, not checked here. The module's DisMech comparison is a methodological precedent only.

content: Any T-type claim attached to a WWOX antiseizure compound derives from an isoform-agnostic catalogue annotation on a drug, not from WWOX biology; the link is an annotation artifact.
note: Repeated four times; the report states provenance only "appears" to be catalogue-derived (L105).

content: On current evidence the reported effect cannot be attributed to any single Cav3 isoform.
Compounds carrying T-type blocker labels are pan-Cav3 and polypharmacological; clinically tested T-type blockers are pan-isoform.
Review quote: adverse effects of pan-T-type blockers in essential tremor trials may be avoided by subtype-specific inhibitors, which remain a development goal.
note: Quote is longer than 25 words in the report; paraphrased here. Review labelled 2018-2025.

content: Mibefradil is a potent cell-surface blocker of Orai (store-operated calcium) channels, a new pharmacological action.
Ethosuximide anticonvulsant action was independent of the T-type channel: a null mutation in worm cca-1 did not affect it.
anchor: L10 Summary; L19 F002; L22 F003; L36; L59
note: Called "most decisive" by the report; C. elegans system. Overreach marker: the report generalises this to 'has been shown to be entirely T-type-independent' (L10); the datum is one worm model, one PTZ assay, one ortholog tested (verifier D11). Sample sizes not rechecked.

content: A catalogue "T-type blocker" tag neither identifies the Cav3 isoform engaged nor guarantees that the antiseizure effect is T-type-mediated at all.
WWOX-DEE seizure semiology: focal 85 percent, epileptic spasms 77 percent, tonic 69 percent.
note: Cohort-level (L107).

content: Established antiseizure role of T-type channels lies in thalamocortical rebound bursting and generalised spike-and-wave of absence epilepsy (reticular-thalamic bursts); review says role of T-type channels, GABAergic inhibition and synchronisation is well established.
Circuit context of T-type antiseizure action does not match WWOX-DEE focal/spasm/tonic semiology, lowering the prior for a Cav3 mechanism.
note: Hedge at L107: does not exclude a T-type contribution.

content: A de novo CACNA1G (Cav3.1) variant caused neurodevelopmental delay and cerebellar hypoplasia with no seizure history and normal EEG.
note: Used to say isoform-phenotype links are not uniformly epileptogenic.

content: Parsimonious default: any antiseizure effect of a T-type compound in WWOX models is general anticonvulsant activity, not isoform-specific Cav3 modulation.
note: Stated as the default explanation.

content: Attribution requires genetics and orthogonal chemistry, not catalogue labels; five requirements listed (selective-antagonist concordance, matching KO cross, inactive controls, allele stratification, direct Cav3 measurement).
note: Umbrella item for E21 to E27.

content: Concordance of effect across structurally unrelated selective antagonists (Z944, Z941, TTA-P2, ulixacaltamide), tested alongside ethosuximide in the WWOX model.
note: Report elsewhere concedes these are not perfectly isoform-discriminating (E70).

content: Cross Wwox-null (and a hypomorphic-missense allele) to Cacna1g, Cacna1h and Cacna1i knockout lines; measure seizure phenotype and drug response; true Cav3.2 effect abolished on Cacna1h KO and retained on the other two.
note: Called the decisive test and the gold standard.

content: Inactive-enantiomer or inactive-analog control, stereochemically or structurally matched, to exclude non-specific CNS-depressant explanations.
note: No specific compound pair named.

content: Stratify biallelic-null versus hypomorphic-missense WWOX models for baseline seizure burden and T-type drug sensitivity; genotype-dependent effect tracks allele class, a general anticonvulsant does not.
note: Called the single cleanest discriminator (L77, L120).

content: Quantify Cacna1g/h/i mRNA, Cav3 protein and T-type current (voltage-clamp) in WWOX-deficient neurons versus controls, stratified by allele class, with and without HIF1alpha inhibition.
note: Tests the F007 bridge directly.

content: Reproduce the drug effect in non-WWOX induced-seizure models (PTZ, kainate); reproduction indicates general anticonvulsant activity.
Frame the controls as pre-registered and decisive; factorial genetic by chemotype design plus allele stratification.
note: Pre-registered appears once.

content: If a genotype-dependent T-type effect exists, the most plausible route is metabolic-stress/HIF1alpha-driven upregulation of CACNA1H/Cav3.2; specific, testable, unproven.
anchor: L12 Summary; L41 F007; L63-72; L103
note: Report says "single coherent route"; labelled hypothesis, not mechanism.

content: HIF1alpha transcriptionally upregulates Cav3.2 (Cacna1h), described as a putative transcriptional target; HIF1alpha activation elevated network activity and hypoxia-induced neuronal hyperexcitability.
note: putative in the quote. System not stated by the report. Audit D03: promoter activity was in NS20Y cells, not primary neurons; species of the primary neurons is not stated in the abstract.

content: Cav3.2 transcriptional induction is a critical step in epileptogenesis in the pilocarpine model; absent in mice lacking Cav3.2, with spontaneous seizures dramatically reduced.
note: Acquired-epilepsy model, mouse.

content: Wwox-null mice carry metabolic stress/hypoglycaemia that is rescued by neuronal WWOX.
note: First link of the proposed chain.

content: Metabolic stress activates HIF1alpha in WWOX deficiency (hypothesised bridge).
note: No source is given for this step in a WWOX context although L103 says each link is individually supported.

content: Biallelic-null WWOX genotypes carry the most severe metabolic and survival phenotype; the null versus hypomorphic-missense split already predicts WWOX survival in the knowledge base.
Prediction: biallelic-null alleles show greatest Cav3.2 induction and T-type drug sensitivity; hypomorphic-missense least; a general anticonvulsant shows no allele gradient.
note: Derived from E31, E32, E33.

content: The HIF1alpha-Cav3.2 bridge is a hypothesis; each link is said to be individually supported but the chain has never been demonstrated in a WWOX model.
note: Internal tension with E32.

content: CaV3.3 knockout mice, and mice with CaV3.3 silenced predominantly in the reticular nucleus, had increased susceptibility to drug-induced spike-and-wave discharges; CaV3.2 knockout also increased it per the report.
note: Quote given names only CaV3.3; the CaV3.2 statement is the report's summary. Audit D07: the paper tests no single CaV3.2 knockout (double knockout only; read through a summary route, moderate confidence; abstract alone consistent). Ethosuximide there is reported only in CaV3.3-/- mice.

content: Isoform effects can be opposite in sign and counterintuitive, so pharmacology alone cannot assign a mechanism to CACNA1G, H or I; a genetic cross is the orthogonal control.
note: - Audit D07: 'opposite in sign' is not shown by the cited paper; it shows that deleting an isoform raised SWD against expectation, not a comparison of two isoforms with opposite signs.

content: Z941 and Z944 potently suppressed absence seizures by 85 to 90 percent via a mechanism distinct from ethosuximide and valproate.
note: Rodent absence model implied.

content: The Z941/Z944 result directly confirms that ethosuximide's effect is not purely T-type.
note: Differs from the worm-null argument (E13).

content: Z944 shows disease-modifying (anti-epileptogenic) activity in a temporal-lobe epilepsy model.
note: Flagged mismatch by the report (L98); abstract-level use.

content: Cryo-EM structures of human Cav3 channels with bound blockers define isoform binding sites, enabling isoform-biased probes.
An inherited CACNA1H variant co-occurs with de novo SCN8A in severe developmental and epileptic encephalopathy.
note: Flagged mismatch by the report (L98); abstract-level use.

content: CACNA1H variants associate with idiopathic/genetic generalised epilepsy via increased channel surface expression and excitability.
CACNA1H excitability phenotype was reversed to normal by either ethosuximide or the T-channel blocker TTA-P2.
note: Cited as published chemotype-concordance template. Audit D12 (moderate confidence, web-fetch summary of the Results; open: one full-text read of the Results and the Figure 5 legend): TTA-P2 was tested on firing (about 66 percent block); ethosuximide was used only in the dendritic growth experiments; neither was tested on the burst threshold. The report's 'excitability phenotype reversed by two blockers' is not supported for excitability.

content: CACNA1H R1584P acts as a modulator of seizure development and expression, a background-dependent modulator rather than a sufficient cause.
note: Matched to the genotype-dependence framing.

content: CACNA1H/Cav3.2 is the prime candidate through 'three independent convergences' (report's wording): HIF1alpha target, driver of acquired epileptogenesis, DEE association and seizure modulation.
note: Not by elimination alone. Audit: the convergences are not independent; the first two sources (HIF1alpha paper, pilocarpine paper) share two authors (Bonn) and one builds on the other; the third is a case report whose authors disclaim a DEE association.

content: CACNA1G and CACNA1I remain possible but are less favoured; CACNA1G channelopathy can present without seizures.
note: CACNA1I has no supporting row anywhere in the report.

content: A T-type mechanism in WWOX would have to operate through a different circuit logic, e.g. acquired Cav3.2 upregulation driving focal hyperexcitability as in pilocarpine, not reticular-thalamic burst suppression.
E1/E2: a true Cav3.2 or Cav3.1 effect; decisive control a Wwox-null x matching Cacna1h or Cacna1g KO cross with Z944 plus TTA-P2 concordance.
note: Prediction: abolished on matching KO, retained for the other two.

content: E3: pan-T-type effect; single versus combined Cav3 KO; partial loss with any single KO, full loss only with combined KO.
E4: off-target polypharmacology; all Cav3-null backgrounds plus selective tools; effect retained on every Cav3-null background and not reproduced by selective probes.
note: Cites the ethosuximide/cca-1 precedent.

content: E5: general anticonvulsant activity; non-WWOX induced-seizure models and allele-class comparison; effect allele-class-independent and reproduced in non-WWOX models.
Non-specific CNS-depressant effect as an explanation to be excluded by an inactive matched control.
note: Side remark.

content: Catalogue-label reasoning is an invalid leap: compound X reduces seizures, X is annotated T-type blocker, therefore WWOX seizures involve T-type channels and then specifically CACNA1G/H/I.
note: Diagram; breaks because labels are pan-isoform, drugs polypharmacological, effect may be T-type-independent.

content: The question is reframed from which isoform mediates the effect to whether any T-type mechanism exists and how an isoform would be proven.
Does any T-type mechanism exist in WWOX deficiency, and if so which isoform and is it genotype-dependent versus general anticonvulsant activity?
note: Restates the prompt question.

content: Which specific compound, WWOX model and seizure assay underlie the "reported antiseizure effects"? Provenance could not be traced.
note: Report asks the user to identify it.

content: First action: identify the reported compound and assay and trace provenance; all other experiments conditional on this.
No primary WWOX experimental data were available; the work is a mechanistic and evidentiary audit that cannot itself demonstrate a T-type mechanism.
Reported antiseizure effects could not be traced to a primary source within the knowledge base; absence of a T-type node leads to the inference that provenance is catalogue-derived.
Semiology data are cohort-level; seizure type does not exclude a T-type contribution, only lowers the prior relative to absence epilepsy.
Isoform-selective pharmacology is imperfect: even Z944 and TTA-P2 are not perfectly isoform-discriminating across Cav3.1/3.2/3.3; selective-compound concordance is supportive, not definitive.
note: Tension with calling these "T-type-selective" (L28) and "selective antagonists" (L12).

content: Two citations flagged as mismatch (PMID:31419467 and PMID:34399820) are used only for claims verified by their abstracts.
note: Report-internal note on citation reliability; the nature of the mismatch is not described.

content: Ethosuximide: classic antiseizure drug, suggested T-type target; used as reference and as the example of T-type-independent action.
note: Proposed as comparator in WWOX model (L116).

content: Mibefradil: archetypal T-type drug, potent Orai blocker.
note: Named as polypharmacology example, not as test compound.

content: Z944: high-affinity T-type-selective antagonist; also anti-epileptogenic in TLE model.
note: Proposed test compound.

content: Z941: selective T-type antagonist, as Z944.
note: Proposed test compound.

content: TTA-P2: T-channel blocker that reversed CACNA1H variant excitability; proposed concordance probe.
note: Proposed test compound.

content: Ulixacaltamide: named as a structurally unrelated selective antagonist to include in concordance panel.
note: Only mention, no source and no property stated.

content: Valproate: named in passing as a comparator whose mechanism differs from Z941/Z944.
note: Side mention.

content: Lithium: abolishes PTZ-induced seizures in Wwox-/- mice (GSK-3beta route).
note: Not proposed as a T-type probe; noted as only drug-linked mechanism.

content: AAV9-SynI-WWOX gene replacement, listed among curated experimental treatments.
note: Side mention.

content: CACNA1H / Cav3.2: prime candidate isoform.
note: See chain C02/C03.

content: CACNA1G / Cav3.1 and CACNA1I / Cav3.3: possible but less favoured.
note: Cav3.3 is named in a KO precedent (E36); CACNA1I has no dedicated support.

content: Orai store-operated calcium channels: off-target of mibefradil.
GSK-3beta: the only curated drug-linked seizure mechanism node.
HIF1alpha: proposed upstream regulator of Cav3.2; inhibition arm proposed.
WWOX loss, metabolic stress, HIF1alpha activation, Cav3.2 upregulation, hyperexcitability, genotype-dependent T-type drug sensitivity.
note: Whole chain labelled hypothesis (L41, L103).

content: WWOX allele class (null versus hypomorphic) as determinant of T-type drug sensitivity.
note: Rests on E78.
